title: Compactly supported direct image preserves D^b_c with Q̄_ℓ coefficients (étale)
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ an algebraic closure of the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the adic coefficient constructions: $D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)$ is the derived-complete integral category with uniformly bounded constructible finite reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $D^b_c(T,E)=D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ is its raw scalar localization with the same objects [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $D^b_c(T,\Omega)$ is the common-stage category of pairs $(E,K_E)$ over finite subextensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. These object constructions are used over $k$; they do not require $k$ to be the algebraic closure of a finite field.

For $K=(E,K_E)\in D^b_c(X,\Omega)$ let $L\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an integral representative of $K_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $L_n=L\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!=Rf_{!,n}^c$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ denote restriction of scalars from $A_{E,n}$ to the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Form the tower $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_n F_nL_n$: its transition is $F_{n+1}$ of the reduction map followed by the restriction-of-scalars comparison [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Then the compact-support value represented by
$$\left(E,\left[R\varprojlim_n M_n\right][1/\varpi_E]\right)$$
is an object of $D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$ for every such representative and compactification; $R\varprojlim$ is the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. Thus the integral-limit, rationalization and common-stage compact-support construction preserves bounded constructibility. This is its objectwise finiteness assertion; independence and coherence of the representative choices are separate assertions.

proof.text: Write $K=(E,K_E)$ by the common-stage definition, and choose its integral object $L$ by the same-object definition of raw rationalization. The compactification has $p:V\to Y$ proper and hence finite type; composing finite affine covers and algebra generators shows $V$ is finite type over $k$. Thus $X,Y,V$ are Noetherian. Opens of a Noetherian scheme are quasi-compact, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Choose its reduced closed complement.

proof.text: Put $B=j_!L$ for completed ringed-site extension by zero. The integral open-reduction comparison applies since $j$ is quasi-compact and $L$ derived complete. It says $B$ is derived complete, and gives $B_n\cong j_!L_n$, commuting with every strict quotient transition. The coefficient identification on the open is included in that statement.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); the strict complete version is the cited integral open-reduction comparison

proof.text: The input reductions $L_n$ have constructible cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$. Ringed extension by zero is exact, so the exact-functor cohomology isomorphism gives $H^r(B_n)\cong j_!H^r(L_n)$ and zero outside $[a,b]$. Extend a finite constructible locally closed stratification of each $H^r(L_n)$ by the reduced closed complement $Z=V\setminus X$. Its strata remain locally closed and constructible in the Noetherian $V$: an open of $X$ is open in $V$, a closed subset of $X$ is the intersection with a closed subset of $V$, and all these opens are quasi-compact. On strata in $X$, $j^{-1}j_!$ is identity, so the restrictions retain their finite locally constant module models; on $Z$, $i^{-1}j_!=0$, so the restriction is zero. This is exactly finite-torsion constructibility. Together with completeness from step 2 and the unchanged interval, the integral-category definition gives $B\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; explicit stratification argument for its open factor

proof.text: Apply integral direct-image constructibility to $p:V\to Y$ and $B$. Step 1 supplies finite-type schemes over $k$, and $\ell$ is invertible because they are $k$-schemes. It gives $T=Rp_*B\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, which by the definition of the integral derived direct image is a derived limit of $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}B_n$ whose transitions are $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ of $Rp_{*,n+1}$ of the quotient reduction $B_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}B_n$ followed by the restriction-of-scalars identification for $Rp_*$, i.e. exactly the transitions of $N_\bullet$ in the tower comparison below. The compact-support proper-image tower comparison applies to the same $j,p,L$ and the canonical comparisons of step 2: its maps $N_n\cong M_n$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems with exactly the transition maps in the statement.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.2 and 6.7.7; proper-image and strict tower comparisons as stated by the cited nodes

proof.text: Exact countable products of completed-coefficient module sheaves and parts (2), (1) of derived-limit existence supply a derived limit $M$ of $M_\bullet$. The system isomorphism of step 4 extends to a morphism of the Roos triangles for $T$ and $M$ by the derived-limit morphism lemma. The levelwise-isomorphism lemma makes $T\to M$ invertible. Isomorphism closure of the integral constructible category gives $M\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; the same argument works for every derived limit in the displayed formula.

source.place: Tag 08TC (Roos triangle); existence and isomorphism lemmas explicitly cited

proof.text: The same object $M$ is an object $M_E$ of the raw localization $D^b_c(Y,E)$, since localization changes Hom groups and not objects. Hence $(E,M_E)$ is an object of the common-stage category $D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$, exactly the displayed compact-support value. This proves membership for each representative and compactification; coefficient coherence and independence are separate assertions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NE-16bb980a1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full; it has no new nodes. Read every cited statement, the main-20261015 def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.6 and 6.7.7, Stacks 0GL1 and 08TC, and the upstream Lean declaration with its constructibility definitions. The statement correction (E7) is accepted. The upstream declaration is about discrete PadicAlgCl sheaves on the étale site, with Y only locally of finite type and not quasi-compact. Its own docstring derives the result by a limit over Z/ℓ^n and inverting ℓ, which is the adic construction. The imported DAG statement cited a finite-ring definition for Q̄_ℓ, which does not type-check. The declaration is also false even with discrete coefficients: take Y = ⊔ Spec k and X_n = the union of the n+2 coordinate hyperplanes in P^{n+1}; then H^n(X_n, Q) = H^n(S^n) ≠ 0, so the direct image is unbounded. The corrected adic statement keeps all hypotheses of the source (finite type, separated f, ℓ invertible, chosen compactification) and is exactly what the citing definition needs. Steps checked: step 1 is the Noetherian geometry and quasi-compactness of j, as in the reviewed integral node. Step 2 is the open-reduction comparison (completeness and strict α_n). Step 3 is the elementary stratification extension (j^{-1}j_! = id, i^{-1}j_! = 0, exact cohomology), the same content as lem-sf-open-finite-constructibility-interval; that node cannot be cited because it would close a cycle through lem-trf-open-ctf. Step 4 is integral Rp_* finiteness plus the tower lemma β_n. Step 5 is Roos-triangle morphism, levelwise isomorphism and isomorphism closure. Step 6 is definitional. The node duplicates lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible in substance, but citing that node would create a cycle (path confirmed by BFS), so reproving it is justified. FIX (C3): step 4 relies on the transition maps of Rp_*B, which are specified in def-weil-derived-direct-image, not in the cited lemma. I added that citation to the step's uses and to proof_deps (no cycle) and wrote out the transition; corrected file at fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-sf-qbar-etale-lower-shriek-constructible.json. All four declared tool_uses are accepted. Small cases checked: K = 0, X empty, j = id, f = id, E = Q_ℓ.
